sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, on 05.09.2022 the informant in his written report has stated that 20 days ago, his Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.371 of 2024(4) dt.13-08-2024 cousin sister/ victim aged about 11 years had gone to her maternal grandmother's place.

Thereafter, her cousin maternal aunt (mami) (Pinki Devi) enticed the victim by way of giving her clothes and on many temptations,
took her to one Vinay Prasad Yadav at Telhara market.

Thereafter, Pinki Devi, victim and Vinay Prasad Yadav went to Ekangar Sarai market in the name of buying clothes and then Vinay Prasad Yadav took her in a room and established sexual relation with the victim.

It is further alleged that Pinki Devi once again on 04.09.2022 tried to take her away by alluring and threatening the victim due to which, on hearing the screams of the minor girl, the villagers caught Pinki Devi and handed over to Parwalpur Police station.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant in Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 371 of 2024 submits that from the written report submitted by the informant (PW-4) in the Ekangar Sarai Police Station, it would appear that the alleged occurrence in which this appellant is said to have been caught by the villagers of the informant took place in village Badhauni within Parwalpur Police Station on 04.09.2022.

According to the informant, the appellant was taken to Parwalpur Police Station by the villagers and she was handed over to Parwalpur Police Station with a request to take appropriate action against her.
It is submitted that Patna High Court CR.

APP ( DB) No.371 of 2024(4)
dt.13-08-2024 no FIR was registered in Parwalpur Police Station and the appellant has not been shown arrested in the said police station
, therefore, the whole story that this appellant had been caught by the villagers and then was handed over to Parwalpur Police Station could not be substantiated in course of trial.
6. Learned counsel submits that the written report has been submitted by cousin brother of the victim girl in Ekangar Sarai Police Station on 05.09.2022.

From the evidence of the prosecution Pinki Devi vs The State Of Bihar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32491590/
2 witnesses, it would appear that PW-1 has stated in course of his cross-examination that his statement was recorded by police at the police station on 04.09.2022 and on the same day, the statement of the cousin brother of the victim (PW-4) was also recorded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He has stated that on the same day, the statement of the victim girl was also recorded in the police station but surprisingly,
the first version of the victim girl, the informant (PW-4) and the witness (PW-1) has not been brought on record in course of trial.
The appellant Pinki Devi was called in Ekangar Sarai Police Station where she was arrested.
7. Learned counsel further submits that PW-1 has stated that he was making a statement on the basis of what he was told about the occurrence.
8. Learned counsel further submits that PW-2 has Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.371 of 2024(4) dt.13-08-2024 stated that the occurrence took place on 06.09.2022 when the victim was weeping and Madam was trying to allure her in order to take her away.
Thus, while PW-1 is claiming to have made statement on 04.09.2022, PW-2 says that the occurrence took place on 06.09.2022.
According to PW-2, the victim had told him that she was taken by this appellant Pinki Devi earlier in the month of August.

9. Learned counsel submits that the appellant Pinki Devi is the cousin mami of the victim (wife of the cousin maternal uncle of the victim) and it is all through the defence case that there is an enmity between own maternal uncle of the victim and her cousin maternal uncle.
It is for this reason that the wife of the cousin maternal uncle has been falsely implicated in the present case.

10. Learned counsel submits that the victim girl has stated in her evidence that few days before the Raksha Bandhan last year, she had gone to her maternal grandmother's place where she desired to go to her village whereupon her cousin mami, Pinki Devi told that she would drop her in her village.
She had come with her mami and mamera bhai and thereafter, her mamera bhai returned.

She alleged that mami called a person and then that person came on motorcycle who took both Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.371 of 2024(4) dt.13-08-2024 of them at a fruit shop in Ekangar Sarai and then her mami took her in a street in a house and then the appellant in Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 385 of 2024, namely, Vinay Pradad Yadav forcibly established physical relationship with her.

It is submitted that from the evidence of the victim (PW-3), it would appear that she did not disclose the date and month of the occurrence and according to her, the occurrence had taken place in a house which is situated near fruit market which is a busy place but there is no evidence of any independent witness to say that the victim was seen in the company of the appellants sometime near Raksha Bandhan last year.
11. Learned counsel further submits that the medical examination of the victim girl was conducted by a Medical Board.

The report of the Medical Board has been proved by the Doctor (PW-6) who has found the age of the victim as 16-17 years and has categorically recorded that there is no evidence of recent sexual intercourse.
It is submitted that the victim had not disclosed the occurrence, which allegedly took place in the month of August 2022, to anybody in her family.

12. Learned counsel further submits that the I.O. (PW- Pinki Devi vs The State Of Bihar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32491590/
3 7) has stated that there is no witness from Ekangar Sarai in this case.

entities.text: I.O. (PW- Pinki Devi vs The State Of Bihar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has also stated that he had not made any verification Patna High Court CR.
APP ( DB) No.371 of 2024(4) dt.13-08-2024 about the occurrence of 04.09.2022 which took place in Badauni

. With reference to this part of the evidence, learned counsel for the appellants submits that if the I.O. has not verified about the occurrence of 04.09.2022 which the informant claims to have taken place in village Badauni, the whole prosecution case would fail.

Learned counsel further submits that the I.O. had not even verified the age of the victim girl from the school in course of investigation and had not tried to know about the motorcycle by which the victim was said to have taken away in the first occurrence.
The I.O. has stated that there is no eye witness to this occurrence.
13. Learned counsel submits that the mother of the victim has been examined as PW-5.
She has stated in her examination-in-chief that her daughter was in Ekangar Sarai on 04.09.2022 and the wrong act was committed with her on the said day.
It is submitted that PW-5 has come out with a completely different story.

If it is her statement that the victim was in Ekangar Sarai on 04.09.2022,
the case of the prosecution that the appellant Pinki Devi had gone to village Badauni which is in Parwalpur Police Station and was attempting to allure her and take her away would automatically fail.

It is submitted that in paragraph '9' of her deposition, she has denied the suggestion Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.371 of 2024(4) dt.13-08-2024 that there is no dispute between her brother and cousin brother meaning thereby, she admits the dispute between her brother and cousin brother.
It is the case of the defence that because of this enmity, the appellants have been falsely implicated.
In her cross-examination also PW-5 has stated that on the date of occurrence, the victim was at her maternal grandmother's place.
In paragraph '10', she has admitted that the victim had received money from Pinki Devi and according to PW-5, the money was received after the occurrence.
In paragraph '21', PW-5 has stated that the victim told her about the occurrence after the occurrence and she had not told her about the purchase of clothes and going on motorcycle to market.

14. In the aforementioned materials on the record, learned counsel in both the appeals would submit that the whole prosecution case suffers from huge inconsistencies and material contradictions which would in ultimate analysis render the judgment of the learned trial court perversed.
Therefore, the appellants in both the cases who are in custody for about two years would deserve privilege of bail and suspension of their sentence during pendency of the appeals.
15. The prayer for suspension of sentence and release on bail of the appellants has been opposed by learned counsel Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.371 of 2024(4) dt.13-08-2024 for the informant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State
. It is submitted that the prosecution has fully supported the case, hence, the appellants would not deserve privilege of bail and suspension of sentence.

16. Having heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for the informant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State in both the appeals, as also on perusal of the records, to arrive at a prima-facie opinion as to whether the appellants would deserve bail or not, we have perused the records.

We find that according to the prosecution, the appellant Pinki Devi had gone to village Badauni in Parwalpur Police Station on 04.09.2022 where she was trying to allure the victim Pinki Devi vs The State Of Bihar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32491590/
4 girl to take her away, the villagers caught hold of her and took her to Parwalpur Police Station.

sentences.text: In course of trial, the mother of the victim has stated that on 04.09.2022, the victim was in the house of her maternal grandmother, the I.O. has stated in his deposition that he had not verified about the occurrence of 04.09.2022 in village Badauni.
No FIR had been registered in Parwalpur Police Station.

The I.O. has not even verified this aspect of the matter in course of investigation, therefore,
the very first part of the FIR about the date and occurrence when the appellant Pinki Devi had gone to village Badauni to allure the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.371 of 2024(4) dt.13-08-2024
victim girl is not substantiated from the evidence available on the record.

17. This Court further finds prima-facie that the victim girl has been assessed aged about 16-17 years,
the enmity between her own maternal uncle and cousin maternal uncle has been admitted by the mother of the victim and even as the alleged rape is said to have been committed upon the victim sometime in the month of August 2022 in a house which is situated near a market place, there is no evidence that she was seen in the market with the appellants or was seen going into the house of the appellant Vinay Prasad Yadav, medical opinion does not suggest any recent sexual intercourse even the age of the victim has not been duly proved as required in course of law, in these circumstances,
we are of the opinion that the appellants who are in custody for about two years but these appeals are not likely to be heard in near future, would deserve privilege of bail and suspension of sentence during pendency of the appeal as also the appeals being that of the year 2024 are not likely to be heard in near future, accordingly, we direct suspension of sentence and release of the above-named appellants in both the appeals on bail during pendency of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.371 of 2024(4)
dt.13-08-2024 with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned 7th Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum- Special POCSO Court, Biharshariff, Nalanda in connection with POCSO Case No. 113 of 2022 arising out of Ekangar Sarai P.S. Case No. 221 of 2022.

20. List both the appeals for hearing on their turn.
